title: Which Timothée Chalamet Character Are You, Actually?
dek: From peach-scented summer romance to cannibal road trip to space messiah — your answers will reveal which era of Chalamet you truly are.

quiz.intro: No wrong answers here — just pick whatever you'd actually do and let the universe (and Timmy) sort you out.

questions.question: It's a lazy Sunday with absolutely nothing on the calendar. What are you actually doing?

answers.text: Reading in a hammock with headphones on, half-lost in my own head
Staring out a window, quietly turning over a decision I can't shake
Trying to invent something delicious out of whatever's in the kitchen
Driving nowhere in particular with the windows down

questions.question: Someone you just met asks what you're passionate about. How do you answer?

answers.text: I don't really answer — it's complicated, and I'm still figuring it out myself
I light up and tell them everything, whether they asked for details or not
I give a vague answer. Some things aren't for strangers
I talk about duty and what I owe other people, not what I actually want

questions.question: Your family expects one specific thing from you. How do you handle it?

answers.text: I politely ignore it and pursue what actually makes me happy
I ran from it a long time ago and never looked back
I resent it, but I show up anyway because someone has to
I want to make them proud, and it's the thing I struggle with most

questions.question: How do you actually handle heartbreak, real or almost?

answers.text: I brace for it, because deep down I never believed it would last anyway
I don't have time to sit with it — too much rests on me
It knocks me sideways for way longer than I let anyone see
I wear it on my sleeve for weeks and tell literally everyone

questions.question: What's your idea of the perfect night out?

answers.text: A formal obligation I'd rather skip but attend anyway
Chasing a feeling that never quite lasts as long as I need it to
A party where I know everyone and can dance all night
A small room, a guitar, and an audience I can't quite read

questions.question: A stranger asks you for help with something a little risky. What do you do?

answers.text: I want to help, but I might let them down without meaning to
I'm in before they even finish the sentence
I help on my own terms, and only if it actually interests me
I hesitate, then do it anyway because curiosity wins

questions.question: How do people usually describe you when you're not in the room?

answers.text: The fun one. Wears his heart on his sleeve
A mystery, even to the people closest to him
Intense. Quiet, until he's suddenly not
Different than we thought. Heavier than his age suggests

questions.question: What's your actual relationship with the idea of 'greatness'?

answers.text: I'm suspicious of anyone who tries to define what I'm 'meant' to be
I don't think about it — I'm too busy just living this summer
I've stopped fighting it, even though I'm terrified of where it leads
I believe anyone can make something magical if they just try

questions.question: Pick a snack or drink order that matches your exact vibe right now.

answers.text: Whatever's fresh from the garden, eaten slowly
Something practical — I don't have time for indulgence right now
Anything chocolate, the weirder the combination the better
Gas station coffee, black, at 2 a.m.

results.name: Elio Perlman
results.subtitle: Call Me By Your Name (2017)
results.description: You're the one everyone underestimates until they get close enough to feel the storm underneath. Critics called Chalamet's Elio <cite index="2-1">a brainy, brooding boy of 17 who falls in love with Oliver, his father's 24-year-old research assistant</cite>, and that's you — quietly brilliant, guarded, and feeling ten times more than you ever let show.

results.name: Paul Atreides
results.subtitle: Dune: Part Two (2024)
results.description: You didn't ask for the weight you're carrying, but you're not putting it down either. Chalamet himself has described Paul's arc as becoming <cite index="14-6">his worst vision, a person still trying to figure out how to protect those he loves while becoming the all-powerful dark emperor of the universe</cite> — and honestly, you get it.

results.name: Willy Wonka
results.subtitle: Wonka (2023)
results.description: You're the person who shows up with an outlandish idea and somehow makes everyone else believe in it too. Whimsical, stubbornly hopeful, and allergic to cynicism, you'd rather build something magical from nothing than let the world talk you out of trying.

results.name: Lee
results.subtitle: Bones and All (2022)
results.description: You've built a life that works by keeping people at arm's length — and it terrifies you how easily that falls apart the second someone actually gets in. Chalamet said Lee's <cite index="20-3">biggest vulnerability is true love, is kindness, so when he finds that... what he sees is terrifying</cite>, which is basically your whole deal too.

results.name: Henry V
results.subtitle: The King (2019)
results.description: You never wanted the throne, the title, or the responsibility — but now that it's yours, you're going to carry it whether you like it or not. Reluctant, weary, and quietly more capable than you give yourself credit for, you lead because someone has to, not because you're chasing glory.

results.name: Nic Sheff
results.subtitle: Beautiful Boy (2018)
results.description: You want, more than almost anything, for the people who love you to be proud of you — and you're fighting a battle most people never fully see. Based on the real Nic Sheff's memoir about addiction, this role is raw, aching, and painfully human, which is basically you on your most honest day.

results.name: Theodore "Laurie" Laurence
results.subtitle: Little Women (2019)
results.description: You're warm, a little impulsive, and incapable of hiding how you feel about the people you love. The eternal charming neighbor who'd rather be happy than important, you throw yourself into every friendship and every party like it's the best one you've ever been to.

results.name: Bob Dylan
results.subtitle: A Complete Unknown (2024)
results.description: You're impossible to pin down, and you kind of like it that way. Chalamet's performance was praised for capturing <cite index="30-1">the interiority of Bob Dylan – his talent, his prickliness, his distance from people, and his quiet ambition</cite>, and you relate a little too hard to the prickly, elusive genius routine.
